sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Egypt 1600–1800: Key Events
sources.note: Met describes 1744 Cairo foundation as a first-floor water dispensary with an upstairs boys’ school and says over one hundred such Ottoman-period buildings were erected.

sources.title: Medical History, Medical Healers in Ottoman Egypt 1517–1805
sources.note: Original research from court and guild records distinguishes physicians, surgeons, barbers, midwives and other healers; care was varied and not a modern universal health service.

sources.title: Medical History, Medical Healers in Ottoman Egypt full paper
sources.note: Full original article includes records of childbirth attended by midwives and medical practitioners organized in guilds.

sources.title: Princeton University, Al-Jabarti’s History of Egypt
sources.note: Cairo historian Abd al-Rahman al-Jabarti chronicled late Ottoman Egypt and the French invasion; his work is Ajaib al-athar fi al-tarajim wa-al-akhbar.

sources.title: Egyptian Ministry of Culture, al-Jabarti manuscript catalogue

sources.title: Journal of Economic History, Trade, Slavery, and State Coercion of Labor

sources.title: International Review of Social History, The Nation and Its Deserters
sources.note: Archival research traces conscription, desertion and strain on men and rural families in Muhammad Ali’s expanding army.

sources.title: International Journal of Middle East Studies, al-Tahtawi’s Ancient History Textbook
sources.note: Original research describes 1836–37 ministry and school reforms, primary and preparatory schools, state printing and translation, and Rifa’a al-Tahtawi’s textbook.

sources.title: Cambridge University Press, Buried in the Red Dirt: Technically Illegal

proposedOverrides.name: Ottoman Egypt
proposedOverrides.summary: Egypt was an Ottoman province from 1517, with Cairo a center of trade, taxes, fountains and scholarship. Farmers managed Nile irrigation and local Mamluk beys contested provincial power. French troops occupied Egypt from 1798 to 1801; Muhammad Ali became governor in 1805. The imported 1715 to 1783 range is just map coverage.

fell.text: In 1805 Muhammad Ali became Ottoman governor and built a new hereditary Egyptian regime after years of invasion and political struggle.

identityEvidence.assessment: Imported label confirmed; border accuracy and actual local sovereignty unverified.

proposedOverrides.name: Egypt under Muhammad Ali’s dynasty
proposedOverrides.summary: Muhammad Ali took power in 1805; his family governed an increasingly autonomous Egypt with new schools, cotton cultivation, canals and an army. Conscripted men and farmers bore heavy costs. The Suez Canal opened in 1869 after harsh Egyptian labor. Debt, nationalist demands and British invasion led to occupation in 1882, while the dynasty itself continued.

fell.text: British forces occupied Egypt in 1882 after defeating the Urabi movement. The Muhammad Ali dynasty remained on the throne.
